title: voice-delegate
text:

title: voice-delegate
text:
A speech-to-speech model (GPT-Live over WebRTC) owns the conversation. Anything slower than a
sentence is handed to a separate LangGraph worker through a single `delegate_task` boundary, and
narrated back when it completes. The user can interrupt at any time: an interrupted task is never narrated
after the interruption is registered. Backend-owned buffers, queues and sessions have explicit budgets; optional telemetry records
backend spans per turn.

title: voice-delegate
text:
Voice agents fail in two ways: they go quiet while a tool runs, or they keep talking over a
result that is no longer wanted. This project shows one way to avoid both:

title: voice-delegate
text:
- **One delegation entry point.** The voice model knows a single tool; the worker evolves and
  is tested on its own.

title: voice-delegate
text:
- **Interruption invalidates work.** A generation counter is bumped before cancellation, so a
  late worker result is discarded rather than narrated.

title: voice-delegate
text:
- **Bounded everything the backend owns.** Sessions, buffers, history, worker steps and
  result size have limits with a documented reason and a documented behaviour on exhaustion.

title: voice-delegate
text:
- **Provider failover with clamped history.** A primary transport failure reconnects to a
  fallback provider and replays bounded text, never tool executions.

title: voice-delegate
text:
- **Measured, not assumed.** OpenTelemetry spans per turn, provider setup duration,
  transcript-arrival wait, delegation duration by status, failover duration; offline evals for scheduling and limits.

title: voice-delegate
voice-delegate
text:
**v0.1.0 is an implementation release.** The hosted [Vercel frontend](https://voice-delegate.vercel.app) and [Railway backend](https://voice-delegate-api-production.up.railway.app/healthz) offer the simulated demo and invitation-protected documentation search; live voice requires a real backend provider key. Sessions, delegation, recovery, observability, invitations, cited search and same-host scaling are implemented. Live voice, Azure calls, measured voice latency and hosted end-to-end acceptance remain unverified.
See the [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) and [production scope](docs/production.md).

title: voice-delegate
text:
See [the live smoke-test checklist](docs/milestones/live-verification.md#live-smoke-test-checklist). CI runs on hosted GitHub Actions, and paid text-worker evaluations are recorded in
[the evaluation verification record](docs/milestones/m9-evals-verification.md); live voice
and Azure calls have not yet been verified.

title: voice-delegate
text:
v0.x tags publish the implementation with documented verification gaps; acceptance-gated tags begin at v1.0.
The full plan covers voice sessions through same-host scaling: see [scope, acceptance and status](docs/roadmap.md).
The table below covers the core features; later features extend them with a controlled
public demo, a complete use case, advanced voice UX and optional scaling.

title: voice-delegate
text:
Optional [public web search](docs/worker.md#optional-public-web-search) runs in the
worker behind the same `delegate_task` entry point. It is disabled by default and
requires a server-side Tavily key. Offline contracts are verified; live search
quality and spoken delivery remain pending.

title: Architecture
text:
The browser owns microphone capture, WebRTC playback, and display-only captions. FastAPI owns
admission, session capability keys, time budgets, and server credentials. The session manager
owns exactly one provider connection per application session and is the sole executor of
delegation requests. The provider adapter translates public wire events into typed application
events. The application runs a LangGraph worker behind `delegate_task(goal, context)`.

title: Architecture
text:
Keeping audio on a direct media connection avoids an application audio hop. A sideband provides
server-side authority without routing the microphone through Python. Backend results enter as
commentary, separate from trusted instructions.

title: Architecture
text:
`OpenAILiveProvider` implements GPT-Live WebRTC setup, sideband events, commentary and finalization.
`RealtimeWebRTCProvider` contains the shared Realtime WebRTC and sideband implementation.
`OpenAIRealtimeProvider` supplies OpenAI authentication and endpoints; `AzureRealtimeProvider`
supplies Azure resource authentication and deployment configuration. Each provider builds its
own default session configuration and declares capabilities, including transcript timing.
The manager uses the provider protocol and normalized events; it does not select Azure models.

title: Architecture
text:
Provider-side speech detection is authoritative for interruption. The browser's local
energy detector is a latency optimisation, not a replacement for provider events.
It analyses the remote audio element's `srcObject` with the same onset detector at a
higher threshold. While unmuted remote playback has measurable speech energy, local
speech-onset interrupts are suppressed to avoid loudspeaker echo cancelling work.
Local detection rearms after 300 ms of remote silence and requires a fresh onset.
Paused, muted and silent remote audio do not indefinitely block local detection.
Provider speech-start events can still interrupt during remote playback; headphones and
real-device testing remain necessary to assess acoustic behaviour.

title: Architecture
text:
Cancellation invalidates the generation before cancelling tasks. Results from workers
that return after cancellation are discarded. A result already sent to the voice provider
cannot be withdrawn, and cancellation cannot undo a completed external action.

title: Architecture
text:
Timeout limits how long a worker result is awaited. It cancels the worker and sends a
short failure message. Provider transmission has its own two-second deadline, outside
the worker execution budget. Noncooperative workers occupy capacity until they finish.

title: Architecture
text:
Only sealed text segments are replayed during fallback, bounded to twelve entries and
2048 tokens. For Live, a speaker change seals preceding segments; reconnect also seals
every trailing in-flight segment. Realtime uses completed transcripts. Tool calls, tool results and
audio are never replayed. History is conversation data, never system instructions.

title: Architecture
text:
A provider stream failure retains the owned session in the reconnecting state and closes
the failed connection immediately. Browser transport failure starts recovery with a new
peer. An authenticated reconnect request consumes one fallback attempt under the session
lock. Azure fallback preserves lifetime and admission limits; stale requests return 409.

title: Architecture
text:
Cleanup reports failure if either provider's finalization was unconfirmed. A lost creation
response can leave an unknown upstream call; no subsequent request can reliably identify
that call for cleanup. Creation requests are never automatically retried.

title: Architecture
text:
All session operations require both the user's invitation and the session ownership key.
A different valid invitation cannot operate the session even if it knows its key.
Shared-code setups remain available for private testing when public demo mode is disabled.

title: Architecture
text:
SQLite records daily quota reservations before admitting a session. Only hashes of stable
user IDs, UTC dates, counts and reserved seconds are stored, never tokens or transcripts.
The single API process needs durable writable quota storage across deployment and rollback.

title: Architecture
text:
Set `VOICE_DEMO_ENABLED=false` and restart to disable new demo sessions with status 503.
Existing close and heartbeat routes retain authorization. Provider-side spend controls
remain necessary because crashes and remote cleanup failures can outlive local deadlines.

title: Architecture
text:
The worker allows four model steps by default and one tool per model response.
Configurable step and duration budgets stop unbounded loops, while token and byte limits
keep delegated results compact enough for narration.

title: Architecture
text:
The offline planner is deterministic, not a free language model. It exercises the real
LangGraph graph and read-only tools with English commands, without provider calls.
Natural-language planning requires the separately configured paid text model.

title: Architecture
text:
With `VOICE_INTENT_CANCELLATION=true`, speaking pauses narration while independent worker
jobs continue. Up to two running or pending jobs occupy bounded slots. Speech alone no
longer cancels work. Explicit task cancellation, session end, enabled semantic decisions
and the existing worker execution timeouts still cancel work. The existing
interruption path and diagrams describe the default mode; this optional path amends it.

title: Architecture
text:
The browser sends owner-authenticated `/activity` reports with boolean microphone/remote
energy states, sequence and transport generation. Fresh observed silence releases one
bounded pending result with a request preamble. Stale reports hold delivery; missing audio
analysis eventually expires the result. Another result waits until assistant audio has been
observed. Provider speech events reset the gate, and provider VAD remains authoritative for
interrupting audio already playing. This is not an acoustic guarantee; live validation is pending.

title: Architecture
text:
The event reader never awaits a worker or classifier. An optional Decider classifies the
latest bounded utterance with cancellation and relevance predicates per active task. A
classification timeout or error preserves work. Jobs survive a transport replacement and
are delivered through the new connection; a detached Realtime result uses a text item,
not an old function-call ID. See [ADR 009](decisions/009-cancellation-is-intent.md) for budgets,
terminal acknowledgements, pricing caveats and the default-off rollout.

title: Architecture
text:
Task duration includes waiting for delivery and stops at the terminal state. The owner heartbeat
separates worker execution time from delivery wait. Consent-based debug files record task
lifecycle timestamps and durations; normal application logs do not contain task text. A `completed`
task means the result was sent to the voice provider, not that its narration was fully heard.
The UI retains last-reported task states after session end; interrupted narration is not
automatically repeated. Transcript bubbles group consecutive segments from the same speaker
without changing the underlying provider transcript events. The backend separately reconstructs
bounded conversational turns across overlapping speakers for recap and worker context, while
keeping sealed provider segments for fallback replay. Delegation context explicitly identifies
the preceding user turn alongside bounded conversation text. Both are untrusted data; the worker
uses the recent topic to resolve corrections and asks for clarification when ambiguous.

title: Architecture
text:
The opt-in Capacitor client packages the React frontend as local iOS/iPadOS and
Android assets; it uses the existing API, invitations, quotas and single voice
`delegate_task` tool. It does not embed a provider key or load Vercel as a remote app.
Native voice is disabled unless explicitly enabled in a test build. Its requests
retain browser Origin checks: the exact iOS `capacitor://localhost` origin requires
`VOICE_NATIVE_CLIENTS=true` and an explicit allowlist entry; Android uses
`https://localhost`. Backend hosts remain unchanged.

title: Architecture
text:
Native backgrounding releases local media and requests session close. Calls do not
continue in the background or automatically resume. The native build has its own
local-asset CSP, keeps native HTTP overrides disabled, and preserves server-side
session expiry as the final cleanup boundary. Offline fake/API checks do not verify
native WebRTC or device audio. See the [mobile preview guide](mobile.md).

title: Architecture
text:
With `VOICE_WEB_SEARCH=true`, the worker registry adds a bounded Tavily `web_search`
tool. The voice model still sees only `delegate_task`. Calculation and project
retrieval remain local. The HTTP search adapter owns a total deadline and response
cap; it does not fetch pages from returned URLs. Failure discloses a fallback to the
bundled documentation. See [worker configuration](worker.md#optional-public-web-search)
and [ADR 011](decisions/011-read-only-web-search.md).

title: Architecture
text:
Web search is a terminal evidence step: the graph rejects any subsequent tool call.
Sources receive stable URL-derived IDs and validated citation indices. Private worker
job responses include a bounded `web_sources` collection; the API validates these
before exposing them through the normal session source panel. Transport validation
and citations do not establish that the external text is true or safe to repeat.
System prompts ship as Markdown resources inside the backend and agent packages,
with server-selected variants matching enabled tools and cancellation behavior.

title: Architecture
text:
With `VOICE_AUDIO_TIMING=true` (default false), the existing WebRTC stream analyser
observes local and remote energy every 20 ms. Remote energy is accepted only while
playback is active and unmuted. Offer-to-first-audio includes setup; speech-end-to-audio
uses the last local energy observation followed by at least 300 ms of silence.
Overlap and interrupted sampling are excluded. These browser observations do not
measure acoustic output or provider-only generation latency and use no transcript timestamps.

title: Architecture
text:
The browser sends numeric samples to the owned session's `/audio-timing` route with
its transport generation. The backend validates the connected state, generation,
finite duration (0–120 s) and a 120-sample session cap. Only the fixed setup/turn label
is exported to OTel; no session identifiers or conversation content are metric labels.
Uploads time out after two seconds, are not retried, and never end the call. If Web Audio
is unavailable, conversation continues with the existing transcript diagnostics.
See the [measurement procedure](milestones/live-verification.md) for exclusions and
[video storyboard](demo-video.md) for the pending cancellation-design dependency.

title: Architecture
text:
The optional demo Compose stack runs a static frontend proxy, the session API with an
explicit fake-provider factory, a separate private worker using OfflinePlanner, and
the existing collector/Prometheus/Grafana stack. A fixed fake transcript triggers
`delegate_task`; worker commentary returns as a synthetic transcript and heartbeat recap.
The browser uses owned HTTP sessions rather than pretending the fake SDP is playable
WebRTC. There is no microphone, generated audio or measured voice latency in this mode.

title: Architecture
text:
Production factories and the public static demo remain unchanged. The demo factory
requires `VOICE_OFFLINE_DEMO=1` and rejects provider keys, paid planning, fallback and
transcript recording. The frontend build opts in with `VITE_OFFLINE_STACK=true`.
Only loopback frontend and monitoring ports are published. A known fixture bearer value
protects the private worker interface from accidental unauthenticated calls; it is not
production authentication. See [offline deployment](../deployment/README.md#offline-stack-in-one-command).

title: Architecture
text:
The private Codespaces proxy may rewrite same-origin browser requests to
`Origin: https://localhost:8080`. The demo persists an exact origin list including
both localhost schemes and its forwarded URL. Route checks, CORS and limiter
rejections use the same `VOICE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` list; the deprecated singular alias
is used only when no list is configured. nginx continues to set the backend Host
to localhost. See the [measured procedure](local-development.md#measured-codespaces-proxy-behaviour).

title: Architecture
text:
`VOICE_WORKER_MODE=decisions` selects DecisionsPlanner inside the same bounded LangGraph
worker. Each step classifies the next action against current tool names/descriptions,
`direct` and `refuse`. Server code builds tool arguments; an unbound text model generates
final prose. The voice adapter continues to expose only `delegate_task`.

title: Architecture
text:
The shared agent-level `Decider` contract supports predicates and choices without an
agent-to-backend dependency. The backend provides the bounded HTTP implementation;
local and private worker factories own and close the planner clients. Cancellation
classification remains independently controlled by its existing opt-in flag.

title: Architecture
text:
A failed classification uses the existing text planner for that step. Refusals stop
without fallback, cancellation propagates, and ambiguous tool arguments require
clarification. Input/output caps, classification and task deadlines, and the graph's
step limit bound both paths. This is verified offline with deterministic fakes;
live semantic accuracy and cost remain pending. See [worker limits](worker.md#decisions-worker-planner)
and the [reproducible comparison](../evals/README.md#planner-comparison).

title: Architecture
text:
The opt-in [benchmark](benchmarks.md) runs outside the product UI. A local Playwright
page sends fixed WAV input through the existing owned session/offer API and direct
WebRTC connection. It observes received playback energy and delegation events, closes
each session, and retains case IDs, input hashes and speech-end offsets, timings, outcomes,
provider/model labels, browser version, run date and source revision/state. Provider keys
remain on the backend; provider/model labels in the capture are operator declarations,
not browser configuration authority. No new application route or voice tool is added.

title: Architecture
text:
The default path uses a local WebRTC tone pair and scripted scorer fixtures. Live mode
requires explicit environment and CLI opt-ins plus a session budget. Its recordings are
local inputs, not bundled user data. A bounded exporter can retrieve timing-only trace
projections from an existing Grafana Tempo data source; the checked-in Grafana stack
still provisions only Prometheus. No queryable trace storage or live result is implied.

title: ADR 002: Explicit lifecycle ownership and finite budgets
section: ADR 002: Explicit lifecycle ownership and finite budgets
text:
Amended 2026-10-24: [ADR 009](009-cancellation-is-intent.md) adds opt-in independent
tasks and intent cancellation. The behavior above remains the default with the flag off.

title: ADR 005: Bounded worker execution with generation-based cancellation
section: ADR 005: Bounded worker execution with generation-based cancellation
text:
Amended 2026-10-24: [ADR 009](009-cancellation-is-intent.md) adds opt-in independent
tasks and intent cancellation. The behavior above remains the default with the flag off.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Cancelling a worker whenever the user speaks prevents useful conversation during slow
work. A second request need not replace the first. Classification mistakes are asymmetric:
keeping an unwanted calculation costs time, while cancelling wanted work loses its result.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
`VOICE_INTENT_CANCELLATION=false` retains the existing single-task behavior. When enabled,
up to `VOICE_MAX_INFLIGHT_TASKS` (default and maximum two) jobs occupy independent slots.
Running, pending and delivering jobs count towards this bound; rejected IDs are remembered
within the existing per-session request budget. A new request never cancels an existing job.
The voice model still has only `delegate_task`.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Speech interrupts provider narration, not worker execution. Explicit `/interrupt` cancels
all tasks, or just the optional `task_id`. Session termination cancels all work. A portfolio
cancellation generation advances only when active work is cancelled; per-job state prevents
cancelling one job from invalidating another. Noncooperative workers retain global capacity
until they actually finish. No result is retried after an ambiguous provider send.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Completed results become bounded pending deliverables. The preamble includes a bounded
excerpt of the original goal; the complete commentary remains within the existing token
and 500-byte limits. Delivery requires fresh browser audio-activity reports and at least
`VOICE_DELIVERY_SILENCE_SECONDS` (default 0.6) seconds of observed silence. Reports contain
only booleans, sequence and transport generation. They expire after one second. Missing
analysis or a suspended browser holds results; it never implies silence. After delivery,
an assistant-audio observation is required before another result is narrated. Muting playback
does not hide remote stream energy. Undelivered results expire after
`VOICE_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 30) and increment an expiry metric.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
A provider speech-start or transcript event also resets the silence window. Browser energy
is a delivery heuristic, not proof of physical silence or an atomic provider playback lock.
Speech can start after a send; the provider's own interruption handling remains authoritative.
Cancellation cannot retract audio or commands already accepted upstream.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Transport failure alone preserves work. A reconnect retains jobs, clears stale activity,
and uses the new connection for pending delivery. Realtime receives an untrusted text item
for a result from the old transport instead of an invalid old function-call output. Cancelled
or expired Realtime calls receive a terminal output without a new `response.create`; Live
needs no corresponding function-call output. Terminal acknowledgements are best effort and
never retried if delivery was ambiguous.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
`VOICE_DECISIONS_CANCEL=false` makes no Decisions calls. Enabling it requires intent mode
and an environment-supplied OpenAI key. `OpenAIDecider` uses `POST /v1/decisions`, model
`gpt-6-luna`, with named `predicate` questions (`type`, `name`, `instructions`). A plain-text
JSON rendering supplies the last assistant excerpt, current user utterance and indexed goals
as evidence. The API also accepts role-based messages; those are unnecessary for this classifier.
Two questions per task ask about cancellation intent and continued relevance. Only cancellation
probability at or above `VOICE_DECISIONS_THRESHOLD` (default 0.85) triggers cancellation.
Relevance alone never cancels. This threshold is a policy default, not a calibrated live result.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Classification runs separately from the event reader. Fragment bursts coalesce into the latest
bounded utterance, with one request in flight per session; stale decisions cannot cancel work.
The timeout defaults to one second, with at most 60 requests/session, at most four questions,
32 KiB input and 64 KiB response. Errors, malformed output, refusals and exhausted budgets
preserve work. There are no retries, new dependencies, or conversation/credential log fields.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Estimated cost counts successful responses' input tokens at a configurable rate, initially
USD 0.10/million (public Decisions pricing checked 2026-10-24). It is not billing: failed
requests, cache write/read differences, regional premiums and long-context adjustments are
not included. Automatic provider caching may apply; no identity-bearing cache key is sent.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
This amends [lifecycle ownership](002-lifecycle-and-bounds.md) and
[worker cancellation](005-bounded-delegation.md) only when the opt-in flag is enabled.
The default remains compatible with existing deployments. The UI exposes IDs, abbreviated
goals, elapsed time and per-task cancellation; it does not introduce another voice tool.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Deterministic fake workers, classifiers, sockets, clocks and browser tests cover continued
speech, parallel work, explicit/semantic cancellation, stale decisions, timeout, expiry and
reconnect. No paid calls were made. Classifier accuracy, audible silence delivery and cross-provider continuity remain live pending; the live checklist must measure those separately.

title: ADR 009: Cancellation is intent; speech pauses narration
text:
Sources: [Decisions reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/decisions/methods/create),
[Decisions guide and pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions),
[Live delegation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-delegation),
[Realtime conversations](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime-conversations).

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
section: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
Date: 2026-11-01
Status: accepted

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
The voice model retains its single `delegate_task` entry point. The worker needs a
bounded source of current public information alongside calculation and bundled
project documentation. External search results are untrusted evidence. The default
offline demo must continue to work without credentials or network requests.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
Use Tavily Basic Search through a small HTTP adapter, without a search SDK. It
returns structured URLs, titles and excerpts and supports an optional domain filter.
Disable generated answers, raw page content, images and automatic search-depth
selection. Use the existing `httpx` dependency, now explicitly declared by the agent
package; its BSD-3-Clause attribution is already in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
Brave offers structured web results and Exa offers search with selectable content.
Tavily is the initial integration choice for the bounded excerpt contract and direct
domain filtering. No comparative live quality, latency or cost benchmark establishes
it as the best provider. The adapter is separate from the planner and voice provider.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
One request has a configurable total deadline, at most five seconds, a 64 KiB
response limit, three results and no retries, redirects or local fetching of result
URLs. URLs must be public-form HTTPS DNS names without credentials or custom ports;
links are not proof of a site's trustworthiness. Optional allowlisting matches exact
domains and their subdomains. Excerpts are clipped to the existing 400-character
source budget, titles to 160 characters and URLs to 2048 characters.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
`VOICE_WEB_SEARCH` defaults to false. Enabling it requires `TAVILY_API_KEY` on the
worker host. Transport, status, deadline and malformed-response failures explicitly
fall back to bundled project documentation, with a disclosure in the worker result.
No results means no supported web answer. Task cancellation propagates rather than
being turned into a fallback answer.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
After web evidence is read, the graph allows only a final answer: further tool calls
are rejected in code. Calculation or project search can precede web search within
the existing step budget. This limits the first implementation's multi-step workflows
and prevents search-result instructions from launching another tool. Final web
answers need valid source indices; citations do not prove semantic accuracy. If later
narration clipping removes every web citation, the task fails with a bounded notice.
Natural-language search is advertised only for model-backed worker modes; the
deterministic offline planner continues to require an explicit `web ` command. This is
not a replacement for the planned moderation extension or a guarantee that an LLM
will never repeat malicious text.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
Both local and private workers use the same configured tool registry. Private job
results carry up to three validated web sources so cited evidence reaches the UI.
The browser receives sources through the existing authenticated API; it never
receives the search key. Voice providers continue to see only `delegate_task`.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
Queries are sent to Tavily and selected excerpts enter the configured worker and
voice provider flows. No full conversation is sent by the search adapter, but a
model-generated query can contain user-supplied details. Operators should enable
search only when that data flow and their provider plan are acceptable. Free
credits are an account allowance, not an application spending guarantee.

title: ADR 011: Read-only web search in the delegated worker
text:
Offline HTTP fakes verify routing, budgets, failures, citations and blocked follow-up
tool execution. Live relevance, answer grounding, paid account behavior and narration
remain pending. The existing offline demo keeps search disabled.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
The repository [Makefile](../Makefile) provides these shortcuts without installing
shell aliases. Run `make` for help; it does not start a server. `make be` starts only
FastAPI with reload on `127.0.0.1:8000`; `make fe` starts only Vite on
`127.0.0.1:5173`. Stop each process with Ctrl+C. Dependencies must already be installed.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
Run `make invite` to print a reusable **local** invitation, then paste it in the UI.
`make be` uses the same code, stored in ignored `.local/dev-invite.txt` with owner-only
permissions. Restart an existing backend with `make be` before using this code.
The launcher binds only to loopback and requires development mode with public demo
disabled. For that process only, it replaces configured invitation/shared-token auth
with the generated local invitation; the original `.env` is never rewritten and
its existing codes are never printed. Direct uvicorn startup still uses `.env` auth.
The local launcher permits both localhost and 127.0.0.1 frontend origins. `make invite`
is an explicit credential-display action; normal startup only prints the command to
retrieve it. Do not use this local code for Railway or invitations to hosted users.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
Backend settings load from the existing root `.env`; process environment values take
precedence. Normal startup does not print API keys or configured invite codes. Only `make invite`
prints the generated local code when explicitly requested.
With no overrides, code defaults are `VOICE_ADAPTER=live` for GPT-Live, `VOICE_WORKER_MODE=offline` for the
deterministic planner and `VOICE_WEB_SEARCH=false`. Existing `.env` values still win
over these declared defaults. See [all configuration names](configuration.md).

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
These model-backed modes require a privately configured `OPENAI_API_KEY` and can
incur provider charges. [Worker setup](worker.md) explains each mode. For persistent
choices edit your local `.env`, then restart the backend. Never put API keys in the
Makefile or frontend variables.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
The frontend shortcut explicitly defaults `VITE_API_BASE_URL` to empty so Vite proxies
`/api` to the local backend, even if a frontend env file names a hosted API. To select
a hosted backend explicitly:

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
A non-local backend must allow the frontend origin. This does not deploy or modify
that backend. Paths are derived from the Makefile location, so linked worktrees use
their own backend and frontend directories.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
Open the repository in GitHub Codespaces, or select **Reopen in Container** with a
Dev Containers editor. `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` builds a development image,
installs Docker-in-Docker and starts the same [offline stack](../deployment/README.md#offline-stack-in-one-command).
No provider key or invitation is needed. Keep all forwarded ports **private**.
Open forwarded port 8080 for the app, 3000 for Grafana and 9090 for Prometheus.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
The post-start hook waits up to 120 seconds for Docker-in-Docker before starting
Compose. It runs after creation and after a stopped devcontainer is restarted.
If startup fails, it prints recent Compose logs and the inspection commands:

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
The script persists `DEMO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in ignored `deployment/demo/.env`, which
Compose reloads for subsequent commands with the same Compose file. No provider
credentials are written. Locally the list contains only `http://localhost:8080`.
In Codespaces it also contains `https://localhost:8080` and the public forwarded
origin derived from `CODESPACE_NAME` and `GITHUB_CODESPACES_PORT_FORWARDING_DOMAIN`.
The backend uses `VOICE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`; `VOICE_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` remains a deprecated
single-origin alias. An explicit list takes precedence over the alias.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
Hosted acceptance on 2026-10-25 found that the port-forwarding proxy rewrites
`Origin` to `https://localhost:8080` on requests to the page's own forwarded port,
and `Host` to `localhost:8080`. Requests to a different forwarded port retained
the original Origin. Setting the rewritten HTTPS origin allowed an offline
session, completed delegation and exported metrics. This is observed platform
behaviour, not a guarantee that the proxy will always rewrite headers.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
To repeat the measurement, stop the frontend container, start a small HTTP echo
server on port 8080 that prints only `Origin` and `Host`, open its private forwarded
URL and send a same-origin fetch from the browser console. Compare a fetch from a
second private forwarded port. Do not print authorization or cookie headers. Stop
the echo server before restarting the stack. nginx still passes `Host: localhost`
to the backend; no allowed-host change is required.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
For example, run this probe instead of the stopped frontend, then execute
`fetch('/probe', {method: 'POST'})` from its forwarded page's browser console:

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
Stop the probe with Ctrl-C and run `bash .devcontainer/start-demo.sh` to restore
the frontend. For the cross-port comparison, forward another private echo-server
port and fetch the port-8080 URL from that page; a CORS error can occur after the
request reaches the probe, but the printed Origin remains useful evidence.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
The offline demo populates operation duration, operations by outcome and
**Delegations by outcome**. Transcript wait, worker cancellations and browser
audio playback require live voice; an empty panel is expected offline.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
The first build may take several minutes; the warm-cache goal excludes cold
provisioning. The reported run did not record creation/build timings or its commit.
If a measured cold start exceeds four minutes, enable a Codespaces prebuild in
repository Settings → Codespaces → Prebuilds, select this devcontainer and branch,
and rerun the timing from a newly created codespace. Prebuilds consume the account's
Codespaces allowance; check that allowance before enabling them. Keep ports private.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
The complete generated reference is [Configuration](configuration.md). Process
variables override `.env`; restart the backend after changes. Keep keys only in the
backend environment. Setting a key does not itself enable the corresponding feature.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
`make be` deliberately uses isolated local invitation auth while retaining model and
feature choices. Public-demo/production configurations must use the normal deployment
entry point; they are rejected by the local launcher. `make fe` uses an empty
`VITE_API_BASE_URL` by default to proxy to the local backend. Override that public URL
only when explicitly selecting a hosted API; it is not a place for credentials.

title: Local development and PyCharm
text:
`VOICE_ADAPTER` is the canonical selector for the existing `live`, `realtime` and
`azure` adapters. It selects an integration, not the commercial provider. The old
`VOICE_VOICE_PROVIDER` name remains accepted as a deprecated alias; if both names
are present in the same source, `VOICE_ADAPTER` wins. Prefer the current instructions
here over legacy template values. Keep your existing keys and change only the
non-sensitive selectors/model values when migrating a local configuration.
